Definition: Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon
BiblicalUsage: Ahab is the seventh king of Israel, son of Omri, who reigns twenty-two years in Samaria — and the Bible’s verdict is that he ‘did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him.’ He marries Jezebel, builds Baal a temple, hunts Elijah, and seizes Naboth’s vineyard — and dies by a random arrow at Ramoth-gilead.
TheologicalSignificance: Ahab had a prophet at his door for twenty years and still chose Jezebel's gods — and the dogs licked his blood in the very vineyard he stole. I believe Ahab is the clearest warning in Kings: a man can hear God's word again and again and still die in his sin, and the word he ignored is the word that judges him.
